title: Connecting to Firebase
summary: Set up Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore for the article API, connect the web app, and verify authenticated article CRUD operations.

contents.text: Firebase setup for the article API

This application can use Cloud Firestore as its article backend. In Firestore mode, the reader loads documents from the articles collection, and the admin editor creates, updates, and deletes documents directly in Firestore. Firebase Authentication protects the admin flow.

items: Open the Firebase Console and select Add project.
Give the project a name, then continue through the setup wizard. Google Analytics is optional for this app.
Open Project settings, select General, and choose Add app > Web.
Register the web app and copy the Firebase configuration object. Keep the projectId, authDomain, apiKey, storageBucket, messagingSenderId, and appId values together.

contents.text: In Firebase Console, open Build > Authentication, select Get started, open the Sign-in method tab, choose Email/Password, enable it, and save. In the Users tab, select Add user and create the account that will manage articles. Use a strong password and do not commit it to the repository.

items: Open Build > Firestore Database and select Create database.
Choose a production-mode database. Select the region closest to your users; the region cannot be changed later.
Create the database. The app creates the articles collection when the first article is saved, so no manual seed document is required.

contents.text: Publish these rules from Firestore Database > Rules. They allow only signed-in Firebase users to read or modify articles. For a public reader with a private admin area, use separate public read and authenticated write rules only after confirming your deployment requirements; never leave the database in test mode.

Open src/firebase/firebase.ts and replace the demo firebaseConfig values with the configuration from Project settings > Your apps. Firebase web configuration values are not passwords, but keep service-account keys and user passwords out of the frontend and source control. The app already initializes Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore from this object.

contents.code:
# .env.local
VITE_DATA_SOURCE=firestore

# Start the Vite app
npm run dev

contents.text: This project reads VITE_DATA_SOURCE at build time. Set it to firestore for the Firebase path; if it is omitted, the app defaults to the local SQLite API. Restart the Vite dev server after changing the environment file.

items: Open the admin page and sign in with the Firebase user created earlier.
Create an article and confirm that a document appears under Firestore Database > Data > articles.
Refresh the app and open the article from its category. Update it, then delete it and confirm each change in Firestore.
Sign out and verify that the Firebase admin flow no longer permits article changes.

contents.text: A Firebase configuration error usually means a value in firebase.ts does not match the registered web app. An auth/invalid-credential or auth/user-not-found error means the Email/Password provider or user account is missing. A Missing or insufficient permissions error means the Firestore rules do not allow the current signed-in user. If the app still calls localhost:3001, VITE_DATA_SOURCE was not set to firestore or the dev server was not restarted.
